verdict.probe_answer: Yes for both arms. The root cause is that gawk treats 'load' as a reserved builtin name (the @load directive/extension mechanism), so using -v load=... collided with it and produced 'awk: fatal: cannot use gawk builtin load as variable name'. Both Arm A and Arm B fix this identically by renaming the awk variable from load to loadavg in the NORMALIZED= assignment in scripts/test-db/select_db_host.sh. Both diffs are a single-line functional change confined to that script; neither touches test/hooks.js or any other file. The only difference is Arm A adds a one-line comment explaining why 'load' can't be used as a gawk variable name, which is a minor documentation nicety, not a behavioral difference.
verdict.rationale: Both arms produce functionally identical, correct, minimally-scoped fixes: renaming the colliding awk variable 'load' to 'loadavg'. Neither touches test/hooks.js. Arm A adds an explanatory comment; Arm B does not. Per WRONG/SMELL discipline, the missing comment in B is not a demonstrated incorrect behavior, so it doesn't constitute a material advantage on a one-line shell fix. Parity.
